( @Kim Morrison ) Email from Sid Hariharan sidharth@axiommath.ai (who ideally could be added to the zulip) copied here:

Dear Ravi and Terry,

Ken informed me this morning of your gracious invitation for Axiom to submit to Palomar. We would consider it a great honour to be involved in this initiative, and I, personally, am really excited to see what comes of it. I couldn't agree more that a centralised, curated list of (auto)formalisations, complete with comparator and formalisation information, is needed.

Ken has already told you about [snipped, not yet public], our first blueprinted formalisation project, which we've endeavoured to turn into a library about [snipped]. We expect it to evolve, which will result in updates to the existing comparator files and potentially the addition of new ones. I was wondering if there is a way we could make this dynamism work with the Palomar setup. I read the section about resubmitting after bumps, which explicitly says that comparator files must not be modified for the resubmitted repository to be listed as a new version under the same identifier. Would we then need to make an entirely new submission each time we add something new? Would we then also need to retract the earlier submission? Are entries indexed by repository or comparator challenge/solution pairs?

It would be great to get some clarification. We are very excited about the prospect of contributing to Palomar, and this information would help us determine the best way to do so.

Many thanks,
Sidharth Hariharan
https://thefundamentaltheor3m.github.io

@Ravi Vakil, first, I think anyone can invite anyone to this channel: just @ mention them in a message, and you'll get a little pop-up asking if you'd like to subscribe them.

@Sidharth Hariharan, I've clarified this text now: it's just the path to the comparator config that must remain fixed across version. That is, submissions are amalgamated into versions of the some record if they share the same github repo and path-to-comparator. You are free to change the contents of that comparator config file.
Thanks! Inviting @Ken Ono and @Ashvin Swaminathan too then.

Thank you very much @Kim Morrison for the clarification! We currently have two comparator files (with an accompanying json each), both of which live in the same directory. We expect to make our announcement tomorrow morning (our time), following which we would want to submit to the registry.
